payload.description:
## Context

`basicly-u2hl.27` landed the controller and the actuator on 2026-08-14 (`95974ec`). Its acceptance
criterion is met and the command works — reproduced independently on merged main:

```text
improve: set point: 4000 tokens (read_cost.SCOPE_FILE_READ_CAP)
improve: sensor:    .scripts/check_module_size.py measured 317 tracked module(s)
improve: error:     69 above the set point, worst first; 2 waived
improve: lanes:     0/1 unlanded lane(s)
improve: selected:  tests/test_supervise.py - 60089 tokens, 56089 over the cap (1 of 69)
improve: dropped:   68 candidate(s) not selected; the next run re-ranks them
```

Two gaps remain, both disclosed by the lane rather than found afterwards. Neither is a defect in what
landed; each is a thing the bead's own framing implies and the narrowed scope could not reach.

## Gap 1 — nothing schedules it

The bead says the loop "runs on a schedule". There is no cron entry and no workflow step, because
`.github/workflows/*` and `basicly.toml` were outside the dispatch scope. Today
`basicly loop improve` is a front door an external scheduler must call, and nothing calls it.

**The wiring credit is circular and that is the tell.** `wired-or-deleted` passes this module because
`.scripts/*` is a `COMMAND_SITE_GLOB` and the controller's docstring names `basicly loop improve`.
The script names the command and the command runs the script. A real schedule entry is what makes
that credit non-circular, and until then the gate is reporting a wiring that does not exist — the
same fail-open shape the plan's own risk table names first.

## Gap 2 — the actuator has never filed a real bead

`dispatch()` is covered with a faked `br.run_br` and was never run non-dry, because the dispatch that
built it was forbidden from mutating `.beads/`. A later attempt to exercise it from the base checkout
was refused by the host's permission classifier, correctly: it writes to the live tracker.

So the `br create` argv shape follows `decompose._create_child` and the body goes through
`policy.compose_body` by construction, and that is **derived, not observed**. This repository's
standing rule is that a closed bead proves code exists and not that a path works, and that entering a
forward path is the only way to learn what it accepts.

The first real run is also the cheapest test available: the controller already selects
`tests/test_supervise.py` at 60,089 tokens against a 4,000 cap, which is a legitimate target, so the
bead it files is work worth having rather than a probe to prune.

## Gap 3, smaller — one property of four

The bead's table lists four sensors: module size, the noqa count, C901, and unmatched test files. The
controller drives module size only. It says so in its own output rather than implying wider coverage,
which is the honest form, but three sensors the repo already owns are unused.

## Acceptance

- When a scheduler entry exists, then `basicly loop improve` runs without a human invoking it, and
  `wired-or-deleted` credits the command from that entry rather than from the script's own docstring.
- When the actuator runs non-dry for the first time, then the bead it files is read and recorded here
  with its id, and it passes the plan gate unchanged.
- When a target is selected under the bound, then a second run before that lane lands no-ops, observed
  against the live tracker rather than a fake.
- If a sensor beyond module size is added, then the output names which property it drove.

## Scope

- `.github/workflows/`
- `basicly.toml`
- `.scripts/improvement_controller.py`
- `tests/test_improvement_controller.py`

## Demonstration

A scheduled run files one lane against the live tracker; its id is recorded on this bead; a second run
before that lane lands prints the no-op line and its reason. Read the filed bead, do not assert it.
payload.title: the improvement loop has no scheduler and its actuator has never filed a real bead

payload.text:
[harness-info] the actuator ran non-dry for the first time, 2026-08-14

Owner approved the tracker write. Both halves of the acceptance criterion are now **observed against
the live tracker** rather than derived from a fake `br.run_br`.

## The dispatch

```text
improve: sensor:    .scripts/check_module_size.py measured 319 tracked module(s)
improve: error:     69 above the set point, worst first; 2 waived
improve: lanes:     0/1 unlanded lane(s)
improve: selected:  tests/test_supervise.py - 60089 tokens, 56089 over the cap (1 of 69)
improve: dispatch:  basicly-j73p filed, labelled improvement-loop
```

## The bound, second run, against real tracker state

```text
improve: lanes:     1/1 unlanded lane(s): basicly-j73p
improve: no-op:     bound to 1 open lane; land basicly-j73p before the next run selects another
```

That is the half the fixture could only simulate. It holds.

## The filed bead passes the real gates

`policy.definition_of_ready(repo_root, "basicly-j73p")` returns `ready=True, missing=()`, and
`plan_record.section_entries` parses all three sections: four scope globs, four plan entries
(integrity `L2`, budget `70000`, no dependencies, a backticked demonstration), and one acceptance
criterion carrying its own check. So the `br create` argv shape and `policy.compose_body` produce a
bead the plan gate admits unchanged, which was previously derived from `decompose._create_child`
rather than observed.

## What the live run found that the fixture could not

The third scope glob is malformed: `tests/test_test_supervise*.py`. It is generated at
`.scripts/improvement_controller.py:179`, which prefixes `test_` to the stem unconditionally, so a
target that is already a test module gets the prefix twice. Filed as its own bead.

This matters more than one bad line. The plan's own section 9.3 measurement records tests as the
larger half of the over-cap population — 42 of 95 test files over the cap, holding the worst
offender — so most of this controller's future targets are test modules and most of its future beads
will carry the same dead glob.

**The glob is inert rather than harmful today**, and the reason is worth stating so nobody
over-corrects: the real file is covered by the first glob, so the lane's scope is complete. What is
lost is that a scope entry matching nothing is a declaration the contention preflight cannot use, and
a lane whose declared scope contains dead entries reads as wider than it is.

[harness-decision] manual dispatch first, cron later - owner 2026-08-14

The bead says the improvement loop "runs on a schedule". The owner takes the smaller step first.

**Build `workflow_dispatch` only. No `schedule:` trigger yet.**

Two reasons, and the first is the one that makes this bead worth doing at all. It makes the wiring
**non-circular**: today `wired-or-deleted` credits `basicly loop improve` because `.scripts/*` is a
command-site glob and the controller's own docstring names the command - the script names the command
and the command runs the script, which is a gate reporting a wiring that does not exist. A workflow
entry is a real, independent call site.

Second, the actuator has filed exactly **one** bead ever (`basicly-j73p`, 2026-08-14, its first live
run). Watching it file a few more under a human's hand before it runs unattended is cheap, and the
one-lane bound means an unattended loop that misbehaves would still only produce one bad bead at a
time - but only if the bound holds, which is itself only observed once.

Note this would be the repository's **first** scheduled workflow: `.github/workflows/` holds
`basicly.yml`, `pages.yml`, `quality-gates.yml` and `release.yml`, and none carries `schedule:`.
Adding cron later is a one-line follow-up on this same file.

CI files are on the confirmation list. This comment is the confirmation for `workflow_dispatch` and
**not** for a cron trigger.

[harness-info] the workflow_dispatch call site landed, 2026-08-14

## What landed

`.github/workflows/improvement-loop.yml` - `workflow_dispatch` only, per the owner decision on
this bead. It installs `br` (the controller reads its one-lane bound off the live tracker even
when it files nothing, so `br` is a requirement of the dry run and not only of the actuator) and
runs `uv run basicly loop improve --dry-run`.

## Gap 1 is closed, and the control assertion is what closes it

The complaint was a **circular** wiring credit, not an absent one, so a workflow that merely
mentions the command would leave the same defect with a second cause. The proof is
`test_the_workflow_alone_credits_the_improve_command`: it passes the workflow file as the
**entire** wiring corpus, so nothing under `.scripts/` contributes, and asserts
`wired.command_findings([("loop", "improve")], wiring) == []`.

Tripped in four directions before it was trusted, because an assertion that only ever returns
"credited" cannot tell a real wiring from an empty string:

```text
as written        credited      (expect credited)
command removed   NOT credited  (expect not)
empty corpus      NOT credited  (expect not)
loop supervise    1 finding     (expect 1)
```

The last is its own test - the negative half - so the corpus is not a blanket pass.

## Why the workflow dry-runs, stated at the site rather than inferred

A live run in CI files a bead into an ephemeral checkout. Persisting it needs `contents: write`
and a push to `main` from CI, which is far past what this entry was confirmed for. Filing stays a
human running `basicly loop improve` from the base checkout, which is exactly the "under a
human`s hand" the owner decision asks for.

## The bound re-observed

Running the workflow`s exact command on merged main:

```text
improve: sensor:    .scripts/check_module_size.py measured 323 tracked module(s)
improve: error:     69 above the set point, worst first; 2 waived
improve: lanes:     1/1 unlanded lane(s): basicly-j73p
improve: no-op:     bound to 1 open lane; land basicly-j73p before the next run selects another
```

Exit 0. The bound holds against real tracker state a second time.

## What is deliberately NOT met

Acceptance bullet 1 reads "runs **without a human invoking it**". `workflow_dispatch` cannot
satisfy that by construction - it is a human pressing a button. The owner deferred the `schedule:`
trigger on this bead and the comment above is explicit that it confirms `workflow_dispatch` and
**not** cron. The deferred half is filed rather than left in this bullet, so a reader does not
score a closed bead as an unattended loop.

Gap 3 (three unused sensors) is untouched and was never in this scope.

## Verification

`pytest -q` 3974 passed - two new. `wired-or-deleted` 39 known findings, none new. `module-size`,
`comment-density`, `ruff`, `ruff format`, and the 9 commit hooks all pass.

## Context

Found 2026-08-14 by the first non-dry run of the improvement actuator, which is what
`basicly-e2mz.6` exists to exercise. A fixture could not have found it: the fake `br.run_br` never
rendered a scope for a target whose name already begins with `test_`.

```text
.scripts/improvement_controller.py:178   f"{path.parent.as_posix()}/{path.stem}_*.py"
.scripts/improvement_controller.py:179   f"tests/test_{path.stem}*.py"
```

Line 179 prefixes `test_` unconditionally. For the target `tests/test_supervise.py` the stem is
already `test_supervise`, so the rendered glob is `tests/test_test_supervise*.py`, which matches
nothing. `basicly-j73p`, the first bead the loop filed, carries it.

## Why this is not one bad line

The plan's section 9.3 measurement records tests as the larger half of the over-cap population - 42
of 95 test files over the cap, holding the worst offender. The controller ranks by distance above the
cap, so most of its future targets are test modules and most of its future beads carry the same dead
entry.

## What is actually lost, stated so nobody over-corrects

The glob is inert rather than harmful. The target itself is covered by the first glob, so the lane's
scope is complete and no file is left undeclared. What is lost is that a scope entry matching nothing
is a declaration the contention preflight cannot use, and a lane whose declared scope carries dead
entries reads as wider than it is - which is the over-declaration the plan already records as the
reason nine u2hl children are band-refused on read cost.

## Acceptance

- When the target's stem already begins with `test_`, then the rendered scope carries no
  double-prefixed glob.
- When any scope is rendered, then every glob in it either matches a path in the tree or is the
  target itself.
- Given `tests/test_supervise.py` as the target, when the scope renders, then it is exactly the
  target, its sibling split pattern, and `pyproject.toml`.

## Scope

- `.scripts/improvement_controller.py`
- `tests/test_improvement_controller.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly loop improve --dry-run` against a tree whose worst offender is a test module, with
the rendered scope read from the output; and a regression test that asserts every rendered glob
resolves to at least one path.

## Context

Found by the `basicly-e2mz.5` lane 2026-08-14 while removing `code-reviewer`, and confirmed by
reading `agents.sync_agents` rather than reasoning about it.

`sync_agents` prunes a projected agent only when a **technology selection** excludes its source. It
never prunes a projection whose source has simply been deleted from the catalog.

So a consumer who already installed `code-reviewer` keeps
`.claude/agents/code-reviewer.md` and `.github/agents/code-reviewer.agent.md` after upgrading, and
`basicly agents-check` never notices, because it iterates catalog **sources** and a deleted source has
nothing to iterate.

## Why this is worse than an untidy file

The orphan is a live agent definition on the consumer's host. It carries the retired contract, it is
matched for delegation by description, and it will be selected in preference to nothing. The harness
side of the supersession works - `roles.SUPERSEDED_ROLES` redirects the retired name - but that
redirect is only consulted when the harness resolves a role. A human or a host that spawns the orphan
by name bypasses it entirely.

It also generalises past this one removal. Every future catalog deletion has the same shape: the
authoring repo goes clean, every consumer keeps the artifact, and the projection gate reports up to
date on both sides. That is a fail-open gate, and the plan's own risk table names believing a gate
because its bead closed as the first risk.

## What the removal shipped instead, so this is not re-derived

The limit is stated in three places rather than hidden: the `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer on `c3cdb33`,
the `changelog.d/basicly-e2mz.5.removed.md` fragment as a manual step, and `factory-loop.md` section
6.3. None of those is a mechanism.

## Acceptance

- While a projected agent has no catalog source, when `basicly agents-build` runs, then the projection
  is removed from every agent root it was written to.
- When `basicly agents-check` runs against a tree holding such an orphan, then it reports the orphan
  rather than reporting up to date.
- Given a consumer tree carrying `code-reviewer.md` in both roots, when the consumer upgrades, then
  both files are gone and no other projected agent is removed.
- When a projection is pruned, then the generated-marker rule still governs it - a hand-written file
  a consumer added is never deleted.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/agents.py`
- `tests/test_agents.py`

## Demonstration

Install into a fresh scratch repo at an older catalog, delete a source, upgrade, and read the agent
root: the orphan is gone and every other agent survives. Then run `basicly agents-check` against a
hand-planted orphan and read it fail. Exercise both; the second is the gate half and it is the half
that was silent.
payload.title: a projected agent whose catalog source was deleted survives on every consumer

## Context

Found by the `basicly-e2mz.8` lane 2026-08-14 and confirmed by hand at main after the merge.

`cli.py:1808` hardcodes one reason for every path `agents.sync_agents` returns:

```text
cli.py:1693   the identical string on the skills path
```

`e2mz.8` gave `sync_agents` a second reason to remove a file - a projection whose catalog source was
deleted. The path printed is correct; the parenthetical is not. A consumer watching an upgrade is
told a technology selection removed the file when the source was deleted instead.

The two causes have different consequences for a reader. *Excluded by technology selection* means the
file will come back when the selection changes, so nothing is lost. *Orphaned* means the source is
gone and the artifact is retired. A consumer who reads the first and means the second will wait for a
return that never comes.

two facts. `basicly-9rv0` was two predicates that disagreed, `basicly-7jb5` was one gate name spelled
three times, and this is one message covering two causes.

source**, so this is a pre-existing shape rather than one `e2mz.8` introduced. That matters for the
fix: correcting only the agents site would leave the skills site lying, which is how a defect class
survives its own bead.

is right and only the build half is wrong. The reason vocabulary therefore already exists; nothing
needs inventing.

  path alone, and the command line prints the returned reason.

  deleted, when each upgrades, then the two removals print different reasons.

assert it.

payload.description:
## Context

Measured twice in one pass on 2026-08-20, by an identical mechanism, on two unrelated modules.
Filed because a second occurrence is a pattern rather than an incident, and because the
instrument that would have priced it does not exist.

**Splitting a module raises the prose share of both halves by construction.** The code divides
and the contract docstring does not: each half still owes a module docstring, and each moved
function keeps the one it had. So the size ratchet and the comment-density ratchet pull in
opposite directions on the same edit, and no arrangement satisfies both once a module is large
enough to need cutting.

Two measurements, both from splits the size ratchet demanded:

- `board_snapshot.py` lost 630 tokens of code and 505 of prose in one edit. It went from 3980 tokens to 2845 and from 47 percent prose to 51.5 - **smaller and denser at the same time**. `board_sections.py`, the half that left, landed at 51.5 too.
- `differential.py` split three ways. `views.py` is five frozen records whose docstrings are the payload: 73.4 percent. `derivation.py` is 52.7.

Four density waivers were taken across the two, after every cheaper reduction was measured
first: prose moved to the module whose code it describes, four stale cross-references the
splits themselves created were repointed, and four restatements of what a test asserts were
dropped. That moved 55.7 and 55.1 to 51.5 both, and it was not enough.

## The instrument that is missing

`check_module_size.py` reports only that a module is **over** its limit. It never reports that a
module is *within N tokens* of one. So a module at 99 percent of its cap is a blocker for the
next lane and reads as green in every gate output, and the cost of a split is invisible until
the lane that needs one pays it.

Measured on this tree the same day: 22 modules sit at exactly 0 tokens of headroom and 41 are
within 25. None appears in any gate output. `mirror.py` at 23 tokens cost `basicly-holhk4` its
declared placement, and `tests/test_handoff.py` at 0 has been rebaselined three times.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Take any module at or near the 4000-token cap whose prose share is under 50 percent.
2. Split it along a real seam, moving code and the docstrings that belong to that code.
3. Measure both halves with `check_comment_density.measure`.
4. Observe both shares are higher than the original's, because each half now carries a module docstring the original carried once.
5. Positive control: measure the original before the split and confirm it was under the cap, so the split is what moved it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a module within a stated margin of its size limit when the size gate runs then it says so, rather than reporting only modules already over - check: `uv run pytest tests/test_check_module_size.py -k margin -q`
- Given a split that trades one ratchet for the other then the pair is reported together, so the trade is visible before the second gate refuses it
- Given the existing 22 zero-headroom modules then the report names them without failing, because they are the debt this measures and not a regression

## Scope

- `.scripts/check_module_size.py`
- `tests/test_check_module_size.py`

## Working Set

- `.scripts/check_module_size.py`
- `tests/test_check_module_size.py`
- `.scripts/check_comment_density.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest -q`

The owner's question of 2026-09-13: we bind basicly to `claude -p` and `copilot -p` only so a subscription pays for the work, and that binding may cost more possibility than it saves. Establish, from primary sources, what two open-source harnesses do instead: pi (earendil-works/pi) and DeepSeek Harness (deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). Answer four things.

1. How each manages context (compaction, persistence, resumption, spill) against what `claude -p` already gives us.
2. How each authenticates: API key, OAuth subscription, OpenAI-compatible endpoint, local model.
3. What each already ships that overlaps basicly (work tracking, plan, guard, workflow, skills).
4. What is left that is only ours, and therefore what basicly should become.

Analysis only. No development. The result is a closed record, not a file.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every claim carries its source and the date it was verified.
- The authentication finding names what is established and what is not.
- The record states explicitly what neither harness ships, with evidence.
- Next steps are listed as separate follow-up work, not done here.
payload.title: Research spike: pi and deepseek-harness against the subscription-bound headless runner

payload.text:
RESEARCHED 2026-09-13. All sources fetched live on that date. Nothing ported, nothing installed.

=== 1. A PREMISE OF THE QUESTION IS WRONG: `claude -p` IS THE AGENT SDK ===

Source: code.claude.com/docs/en/headless, fetched 2026-09-13. Its title is "Run Claude Code
programmatically" and its first line reads "Use the Agent SDK to run Claude Code programmatically
from the CLI, Python, or TypeScript." The same page: "To drive the same agent loop from another
language, run the CLI as a subprocess with the `-p` flag and `--output-format json`."

So `-p` is not a degraded mode beside an SDK. It is the sanctioned way to drive the SDK from a
language that is not Python or TypeScript. basicly is Python, so we could use the library; see
finding 3 for why we must not.

What `-p` already offers that we treat as missing:
- `--resume <session_id>` and `--continue` carry a conversation across dispatches.
- `--output-format json` returns `session_id`, `total_cost_usd` and a per-model cost breakdown.
- `--json-schema` returns schema-validated output in a `structured_output` field.
- `--append-system-prompt`, `--append-system-prompt-file`, `--system-prompt`, `--settings`,
  `--agents <json>`, `--mcp-config`, `--plugin-dir`.
- `--permission-mode auto|dontAsk|acceptEdits` and `--permission-prompts none` for unattended runs.
- `stream-json` carries `system/init` (model, tools, mcp_servers, plugin_errors, mcp_server_errors)
  and `system/api_retry`.

AND WE ALREADY RESUME. src/basicly/runner.py:350 emits `--resume <id> --fork-session`;
`RESUME_FORK_FLAGS` at line 66 and `record_session_seed` at line 322 persist a seed per feature and
family. The claim "we throw context away on every dispatch" is false for the claude adapter. What is
true is the price: a prior measurement in this repo put `--fork-session` at about ten times the cost
on a corpus because the forked prefix is not cache-shared.

=== 2. A DATED COST EVENT IS ALREADY SCHEDULED AGAINST US ===

Same source, on `--bare`:
  "Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY before running it, because bare mode doesn't use your subscription login."
  "In bare mode, Claude Code never reads OAuth credentials or the system keychain."
  "`--bare` is the recommended mode for scripted and SDK calls, and will become the default for `-p`
   in a future release."

Read those three together. The day `--bare` becomes the default for `-p`, every basicly dispatch
stops billing the subscription and starts billing the API, silently, at API rates. Our runner does
not pass `--bare` today and does not pin against it either. This is the single most actionable
finding in the spike and it is a scheduled regression, not a hypothetical.

Secondary consequence: `--bare` also skips hooks, skills, subagents, plugins, MCP and CLAUDE.md.
Our whole guidance projection is exactly what bare mode refuses to load. If we ever adopt bare mode
for determinism we must pass the catalog back in by flag, which is what the page's own table
describes.

=== 3. THE AGENT SDK LIBRARY CANNOT SPEND A SUBSCRIPTION ===

Source: code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview, fetched 2026-09-13, verbatim:
  "Unless previously approved, Anthropic does not allow third party developers to offer claude.ai
   login or rate limits for their products, including agents built on the Claude Agent SDK. Use the
   API key authentication methods described in the Quickstart instead."

So the move "leave `-p`, adopt the Python Agent SDK, manage context properly" buys nothing we do not
already have and costs the subscription. The subprocess CLI is the subscription path. That resolves
the owner's "`-p` is a mistake" concern in the opposite direction from the one expected.

=== 4. PI (earendil-works/pi, was badlogic/pi-mono; the old name redirects) ===

MEASURED 2026-09-13 with `gh api repos/earendil-works/pi`: MIT, TypeScript, 104,554 stars, pushed
2026-09-13, not archived. Sources: the repo page and packages/coding-agent/README.md and
packages/ai/README.md, all fetched 2026-09-13.

Packages: `pi-coding-agent` (interactive CLI), `pi-agent-core` (agent runtime, tool calling, state
management), `pi-ai` (unified multi-provider LLM API), `pi-telemetry`, `chord`.

CONTEXT. Sessions auto-save to `~/.pi/agent/sessions/` as JSONL. "Each entry has an id and parentId,
enabling in-place branching without creating new files." Compaction is manual with `/compact
<instructions>` and automatic on overflow. Stated honestly: "Compaction is lossy. The full history
remains in the JSONL file; use /tree to revisit." Resume with `pi -c`, `pi -r`, `--session <path|id>`.
This is the same shape as Claude Code's transcript plus resume. It is not better; it is open.

AUTH, THE REASON THIS SPIKE EXISTS. 30+ providers. Resolution order: explicit per-request credential,
then a `CredentialStore`, then environment variables, then ambient sources such as AWS profiles or
gcloud ADC. Verbatim: "Every provider owns its auth: how API keys resolve ... and, where supported,
OAuth login/refresh flows."

THREE providers support subscription OAuth through `/login`: Anthropic Claude Pro/Max, OpenAI
ChatGPT Plus/Pro for the Codex models, and GitHub Copilot. That is the capability the owner asked
about: one harness, open models by API key AND the existing subscriptions by OAuth.

TOOLS. Four built-ins: read, write, edit, bash, plus grep, find, ls and powershell on Windows.
`pi.registerTool({ name: "deploy", ... })` from a TypeScript extension, and an extension may replace
a built-in outright. CLI selection with `--tools`, `--exclude-tools`, `--no-builtin-tools`,
`--no-tools`.

SKILLS. The Agent Skills standard, loaded from `~/.pi/agent/skills/`, `.agents/skills/`,
`.pi/skills/`. WE ALREADY PROJECT TO `.agents/skills`. A pi target in our catalog is close to free.

EXTENSIONS. Custom tools, subagents, plan mode, custom compaction and summarization, permission gates
and path protection, git checkpointing and auto-commit, sandbox execution, MCP. Event hooks with
`pi.on("tool_call", async (event, ctx) => {...})`.

WHAT PI REFUSES TO DO, in its own Philosophy section: "No built-in to-dos. They confuse models. Use a
TODO.md file, or build your own with extensions." No work tracking. No acceptance-criteria
verification. And from the repo page: it "does not include a built-in permission system", with
containerization recommended instead.

RISK, NOT RESOLVED: pi's Anthropic OAuth is precisely what the Agent SDK page says third-party
developers may not offer "unless previously approved". Whether pi holds that approval is NOT
ESTABLISHED by this spike, and pi's own documentation carries no terms-of-service note either way.
Do not make a product commitment to pi's Claude login before asking Anthropic directly. Its API-key
and open-model paths carry no such question.

=== 5. DEEPSEEK HARNESS (deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness, CLI `dsh`) ===

MEASURED 2026-09-13 with `gh api repos/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness`: MIT, TypeScript, 222,129 stars,
pushed 2026-09-11. Published 2026-08-13 per secondary reporting, which is the one figure here that is
not primary. Sources: README.md, AGENTS.md, docs/architecture.md and eleven package READMEs read
through the GitHub contents API on 2026-09-13.

ARCHITECTURE. Built on Cordis: "plugins contribute services, typed events, and reversible effects to
a shared context." There is no privileged core. The model adapter, the tool registry, the session log
and the agent loop itself are each a replaceable plugin. Composition is by profile and bundle:
`dsh-base` plus `dsh-web-app`, `dsh-headless`, `dsh-sdk-app`, `dsh-acp-app`. Config is `cordis.yml`
with validated fields and "no hardcoded tunables in plugins".

THE SESSION INVARIANT, THE BEST IDEA IN EITHER PROJECT. From AGENTS.md, verbatim: "Model-visible
<=> logged: anything

=== 6. WHAT NEITHER HARNESS SHIPS, WHICH IS WHAT BASICLY IS ===

Both pi and dsh stop at the session boundary. Their state is per session, on one machine, under a
home directory. Neither ships any of the following, and I looked for each by name in the package
list and the docs index:

- A work record in the repository carrying acceptance criteria that a gate reads. dsh's `goal` is
  the nearest thing and it is one objective per session, not a graph the repo owns. pi refuses the
  category outright.
- Verification and validation bound to that record, so a phase cannot advance without evidence.
- Commit-time git hooks. Both gate the agent. Neither gates the artefact, so neither holds for a
  human, for a second agent, or for CI. basicly has 24 hook scripts under .basicly/core/hooks.
- One catalog projected into several agent families. pi and dsh each configure themselves.
- Install and upgrade convergence that preserves a consumer's overlay.

This is the same verdict recorded for claude-code-harness on basicly-u2hl.38 on 2026-08-09, reached
against two much larger projects: a live competitor on the gating and orchestration axes, a
non-competitor on the tracker and projection axes.

It is also the third and fourth independent instance of the design we chose on 2026-07-30 and
recorded at architecture.md:86-106 - phases as engine code, not configuration. dsh makes the agent
loop a plugin; pi makes it an extension point. Neither derives a phase from a committed graph.

=== 7. THE ECONOMIC QUESTION, RESTATED SO IT CAN BE ANSWERED ===

The owner's figure, that the API costs 10x to 20x a subscription for the same work, is the owner's
estimate and is NOT MEASURED in this spike.

Today there are exactly three ways to spend a subscription on agent work:
  a. the interactive CLI, which agent teams now cover well and which cannot run unattended;
  b. `claude -p` without `--bare`, which is what we do, and which finding 2 puts on a clock;
  c. a third-party OAuth login such as pi's, whose permission is unresolved per finding 3.

Only (c) also reaches open-weight models, and (c) is the one with legal exposure. That is the whole
trade, stated plainly.

The comparison that actually decides the product is NOT "subscription versus Anthropic API". It is
"subscription versus an open-weight API". An open-weight model bought by API key has no subscription
to lose, so the 10-20x multiplier does not apply to it at all. We have a lane measured at about
33.2M tokens; priced against DeepSeek or another open-weight endpoint that becomes a number instead
of an argument. That measurement is not done and is the first follow-up below.

=== 8. FOLLOW-UPS. NONE OF THIS WAS DONE; NO DEVELOPMENT IN THIS SESSION ===

a. Pin the runner against the announced `--bare` default flip, and add a gate that fails if a
   dispatch would bill the API. This is a dated cost regression with our name on it. Highest value,
   smallest change, do it first.
b. Price one real lane's measured token count against an open-weight API endpoint, next to the
   subscription. Until that number exists, harness portability is a preference, not a decision.
c. Establish whether pi holds Anthropic's prior approval for Claude Pro/Max OAuth. Ask Anthropic;
   do not infer it from the fact that pi ships it.
d. Decide whether the runner seam should gain `dsh` as an adapter. dsh is a library with a documented
   plugin seam, not a CLI, so it is a different kind of adapter from codex and copilot. Note that
   our runner has never once dispatched codex or copilot: `basicly health` on 2026-09-13 measures 561
   claude runs and 200 manual runs, and zero for both. Adding a fourth unexercised adapter repeats a
   mistake rather than fixing one.
e. Adopt two dsh ideas regardless of which harness wins, because both are ours to build and neither
   requires leaving Claude: `spill` (return a locator and retrieval guidance instead of inlining a
   large tool result) and the invariant "model-visible <=> logged".

=== LIMITS OF THIS SPIKE ===

- No code was run from either project. Every claim about pi and ds

payload.description:
## Context

A dispatch line names the runner adapter and nothing about the model that will actually do the
work. From `_print_dispatch` in `src/basicly/cli.py` the operator gets:

```
dispatch: basicly-jr0l.40 via claude - finished; ready to land, context 106478 tokens
```

"via claude" is the adapter name, not a model. The operator cannot tell which tier was requested,
which model id it resolved to, or whether the host honoured it -- and tier resolution is the whole
point of the models map and the injection kit. A run that silently resolved to a cheaper or dearer
model than intended is indistinguishable from a correct one at the surface.

The data is partly there already. The run record carries `model`, `model_tier`, `model_source`,
`tier_honoured`, `model_mismatch` and `observed_models`. Measured on the 2026-08-01 supervised
run of basicly-jr0l.40, though, the declared half was empty and only the observed half had
content:

```
"model": null, "model_tier": null, "model_source": null, "tier_honoured": null,
"observed_models": ["claude-haiku-4-5", "claude-opus-5"]
```

So the record proves two models were used, and neither the dispatch line nor the record says
which tier was asked for. Note also that `observed_models` is only knowable after the run, while
tier and model id are knowable before it -- the two halves belong at different moments.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a lane is dispatched when the supervisor prints its dispatch line then that line names
  the issue, the requested model tier, the resolved model id and its source, and on completion
  reports the models actually observed together with whether the requested tier was honoured

payload.description:
## Context

Found 2026-08-20 by the lane extracting a helper out of a module at its size cap. Its first measurement
of the extracted unit was an instrument fault, not a result.

`check_comment_density.prose_tokens` returns 0 for a source fragment that does not `ast.parse`. A loose
slice of a module - a docstring section, a function lifted out of its class, anything not a valid module
on its own - therefore measures as 0 percent prose, which reads as pure code.

That is the most dangerous possible wrong answer here, because the two ratchets pull opposite ways: an
extraction is only safe when the extracted unit is prose heavier than the module it leaves, and an
instrument reporting every fragment as 0 percent prose says the opposite of the truth every time. A lane
trusting it extracts the wrong cut, and the comment density gate then refuses the module it was trying
to relieve.

The lane caught it by deriving the number a second way, on a path sharing no step, and getting 66 percent
against 0. The rule it drew is the one to encode: do not measure an extracted unit as a raw slice - parse
it as the module it will become, or refuse to answer.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Take any valid Python module and slice out a fragment that is not itself parseable, for example a docstring section or an indented method body.
2. Call `check_comment_density.prose_tokens` on the fragment.
3. Observe it returns 0, so the fragment reads as 0 percent prose.
4. Call the same function on the whole module and observe a non zero share, which is the positive control that the function works on valid input.
5. Observe there is no error and no way for the caller to tell that 0 from a genuine absence of prose.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a source fragment that does not parse when its prose share is requested then the instrument refuses rather than answering zero - check: `uv run pytest tests/test_check_comment_density.py -k unparseable -q`
- Given a valid module then the share is unchanged so existing measurements keep their meaning

## Scope

- `.scripts/check_comment_density.py`
- `tests/test_check_comment_density.py`

## Working Set

- `.scripts/check_comment_density.py`
- `tests/test_check_comment_density.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest -q`
payload.title: the prose share instrument reports zero on a fragment it cannot parse so an extracted unit measures as pure code

payload.text:
Closed by 67583ec0. prose_tokens raises RatchetError naming the remedy; the whole-tree path keeps its tolerance in tracked_modules. Both halves mutation-tested against a clean base: restoring 'return 0' fails the refusal test, and removing the tolerance fails the tolerance test. Full verify PASS, 31 checks, 4469 tests.

I got one thing wrong and it nearly landed a worthless test. My first run of mutation 2 was applied on top of mutation 1 without restoring, so prose_tokens was still returning 0 and the tolerance test passed. I read that as 'the test does not discriminate'. Restoring first and re-running showed the correct failure. A mutation test needs a clean base and I did not give it one.

Verified rather than assumed: the old test's rationale - a syntax error is ruff's finding, not a reason this gate cannot run - is real but narrower than it reads. verify --mode full runs all 31 checks rather than stopping at the first, and ruff runs before this gate, so the tolerance prevents a second failure report for one cause. It is not needed for the gate to be able to run. That is why the tolerance stayed and why it lives in tracked_modules rather than in measure: a lane measuring a fragment must still be refused, and measure is the surface it would reach for.

Scope widened by three files beyond the two declared, each forced. tests/test_check_comment_density_fragments.py, because the test module reached 4064 against the 4000 cap - recorded on basicly-8ro0nx as its third live instance, with the split priced. docs/plan/implementation-plan.md, because the new file moved a generated count 204 to 205 and every docs-claims consumer test reads the committed tree, so one stale row failed ten tests. The changelog fragment, because the scope names the shipped surface.

Not done: nothing measures whether an extracted unit is prose-heavier before a lane cuts. The instrument now refuses to lie, which is not the same as answering the question a lane actually has.

payload.description:
## Context

Owner question via the orchestrator, 2026-11-12; handily record handily-mn45wh waits for it. The pre-commit hook .basicly/core/hooks/secret-scan.py (rule generic-secret-assignment, lines 31-38) blocks a generated JSDoc line in handily: <redacted:generic-secret-assignment> matches the keyword token, a colon and a quoted value of 8 or more characters. The placeholder filter (lines 41-44) does not skip it. The only ways out today are the inline pragma: allowlist secret (line 9), which turns off every rule on the line and is lost when a generated file is regenerated, and BASICLY_SECRET_EXCLUDE, a path regex that agents may not widen.

## Goal

A narrow, visible allow entry for one finding of the generic rule.

## Acceptance

- When secret-scan refuses a generic-secret-assignment finding, it shall print the path and a sha256 of the matched line, and the allow entry that would accept it.
- When a tracked allow file lists that path and line hash for generic-secret-assignment, secret-scan shall accept that one finding and still refuse every other rule on the line and every other line.
- When the line changes, its hash changes and the scan refuses it again.
- Each allow entry shall carry a reason, so the diff that adds it is reviewable.
- A test shall hold the secret rule tables of the hook, src/basicly/redact.py and the kit redact.py equal, or name each intended difference; today the hook checks placeholders across the whole line and the redactors only the match.
- Proof: input the handily JSDoc line in a fixture repository; action commit, add the printed allow entry, commit again; pass when the first commit is refused with the hash, the second passes, and a real-looking token on another line is still refused.

## Options weighed

- (a) Per-finding allow list, recommended. Leak path: a reviewer approves an entry without reading the line, since the entry holds a hash and not the text; a hash of a short guessable password can be brute-forced. Keep the rule scope to generic-secret-assignment and require a reason.
- (b) Skip a quoted plain lowercase identifier: rejected. It lets real lowercase passwords through (tests/test_redact.py pins such values as secrets), and the scanner sees single diff lines, so it cannot tell a comment from code.

## Size and release

About 30 lines in the hook and 40 lines of tests, plus the shipped_core manifest. A consumer gets it only after a basicly release, which the owner approves.
payload.title: Allow one secret-scan finding by path and line hash instead of a path exclusion

payload.text: Decided by the orchestrator, 2026-11-12: option (a) accepted, option (b) rejected. Conditions: (a) an entry applies only to generic-secret-assignment, never to a specific key-format rule; (b) the refusal prints the exact entry and says a person must read the line first; (c) an entry that matches nothing fails the scan with a named error; (d) a minimum value length for allowing by hash, number and reason to be stated (open, see the correction below); parity test for the hook, src/basicly/redact.py and the kit redact.py, listing each difference before any change and never loosening the hook. Timing: built in lane B's wait for .43.16 if it edits no M5 lane file; release approval stays with the owner. Correction to my earlier leak path: the hash of a short password is not a brute-force risk, because an allowed line is committed in plain text anyway; the real risk is only that a person allows a real secret. So (d) needs a different reason or should be dropped; asked the orchestrator.

payload.description:
## Context

Found 2026-07-31 by the tool-name investigation (see basicly-8sxf's comments for the full measured
report). This is a hardening gap in our own validator, not in a third party.

`src/basicly/agents.py` defines `WRITE_TOOLS = frozenset({"Edit", "Write", "MultiEdit",
"NotebookEdit"})` and matches it by an exact, case-SENSITIVE set intersection to decide whether an
agent declaring a read-only posture is actually read-only.

Measured against GitHub's published alias table
(`docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/custom-agents-configuration`): copilot's tool aliases are
explicitly **case insensitive**, and its `edit` primary accepts `Edit`, `MultiEdit`, `Write` and
`NotebookEdit`. So a catalog source declaring `edit`, `write`, `create` or `notebookedit` in lowercase
would:

- pass our read-only posture check, because none of those strings is in `WRITE_TOOLS`; and
- be granted real file-writing tools on copilot, because the alias resolves case-insensitively.

Our own authoring convention is PascalCase, and `catalog lint` plus review make a lowercase
declaration unlikely today, so this is latent rather than live. It is still the exact class of defect
the posture check exists to prevent, and the fix is small.

Two adjacent facts from the same investigation worth handling here or recording as out of scope:

- `MultiEdit` is **no longer** on Claude Code's published tool list, though copilot still accepts it as
  an alias. Keeping it in `WRITE_TOOLS` is harmless and still correct for copilot.
- `NotebookEdit` alone resolves on the copilot CLI to **both** `create` and `edit` - general filesystem
  write. So the narrowest notebook-only write tool on claude becomes full write on copilot. We do not
  ship it, and this check would reject it in a read-only agent, but the asymmetry is worth a comment so
  a future author does not assume tool breadth is preserved across families.

## Steps to Reproduce

- Author an agent source declaring a read-only posture and `tools: [Read, edit]` (lowercase `edit`).
- Run `basicly catalog lint`.
- Observed: the read-only posture check passes, because `"edit"` is not in `WRITE_TOOLS`.
  Expected: it fails, because the declared tool grants writes on at least one supported family.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given an agent source that declares a read-only posture and a write-granting tool named in any
  casing when the agent lint runs then it fails naming the tool and the posture, and given the same
  source with only read tools in any casing then it passes, with tests

## Context

Reported by the operator 2026-08-22: "we have the id, priority and description, but we do not have a feature or epic name that is descriptive for the human. I cannot distinguish what each of these work items is implementing as I do not know with which feature it is connected."

A wall row today is `P1 | basicly-a4q3.10 | Carry a ranked kill list and its discriminator on a change summary`. Nothing on it says which feature that serves.

## The fact is already on the wire

Measured against the live `/snapshot.json` on 2026-08-22:

```text
parent-child edges in graph.edges : 544
distinct parents they resolve to  : 19, of which 15 are epic and 4 are feature
ready units                       : 187
  resolve to a parent             : 145  (77%)
  orphans with no parent at all   : 42   (23%)
```

The edge direction is `from` = child, `to` = parent. `units[]` already carries `title` and `type` for each of those parents. So the epic a row belongs to needs **no new producer field** - it is a fold over two arrays the document already serves.

The fourteen roots that own the ready set, by how many ready descendants each has: `e2mz` 37, `jr0l` 26, `u2hl` 20, `vkh0` 17, `tcmy` 16, `a4q3` 9, `imnu` 4, `u6jq` 3, `ze8z` 3, `a3ab` 3, `m4zv` 2, `kjc5` 2, `rn0o` 2, `agzx` 1.

## Why grouping rather than a column

Fourteen groups over 187 rows. A per-row epic column repeats the same long title 37 times for one epic and costs horizontal width the title needs. A group heading states it once. The 42 orphans become their own group, which makes a second fact visible that a column would hide: a quarter of the ready set is attached to no feature at all.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the wall renders a ready set, IT SHALL group the rows under the epic or feature each resolves to, and each heading SHALL carry that parent's own title and its ready count.
- WHEN a unit resolves to no parent, IT SHALL appear under one heading that names it as unattached, with a count.
- WHEN a chain has more than one level, THE HEADING SHALL name the root ancestor, not the immediate parent.
- WHEN the graph holds a cycle, THE FOLD SHALL terminate and the affected unit SHALL be reported as unattached rather than looping.
- WHERE grouping is applied, THE URGENCY ORDER THE WALL ALREADY RANKS BY SHALL be preserved within each group and SHALL decide the order of the groups themselves.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_wall.py`
- `tests/test_board_wall.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `120000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: Render the live board and read the wall, checking that a row under a heading names an epic whose id is the root ancestor of that row's id in `graph.edges`, and that the unattached group's count matches the orphan count computed from the same document.

payload.text:
[measurement correction 2026-08-22] The 544-edge figure in the description was read off the SERVED document's graph.edges, which board_snapshot.py:300 filters to edges touching the drawn set. The ledger holds 688 distinct parent-child edges (697 raw events, 9 re-assertions, no record has two parents, zero parent-child retractions ever). Re-measured against the ready set: 149 of 188 resolve to an epic or feature root, 43 are orphans, and 39 of those have no epic ancestor at any depth. No cycles exist today.

THE TRAP THIS RECORD MUST AVOID: build the child-to-parent map from the PRE-FILTER edges list at board_snapshot.py:291, never from document['graph'], or a chain passing through a closed intermediate ancestor breaks and the row silently reports the wrong epic or none.

COST: no extra ledger read is needed. board_snapshot._read_and_fold (board_snapshot.py:157-178) already extracts every live edge as (source, kind, target) triples via board_sections.edge_triples in the same single fold that produces units and titles, and the root titles come from the records already bound at board_snapshot.py:175. The root walk is dict-chasing over data already in memory, memoisable across shared ancestors. That is cheaper than loop_state.phase_map, which needs a second all_views fold this path does not otherwise make.

NO SHORT LABEL EXISTS. There is no component, epic, code or short-name field on any record. Only 31 percent of open records carry any label and the values in use are phase and wave tags. The resolved root's own title is the only answer, so the design must handle long titles rather than hope for a short one.

The row shape to widen is Item at board_wall.py:144-150, which carries priority, ident and title and nothing else; it is built at board_regions.py:315-319.

[scope correction 2026-08-22] The declared scope named board_wall.py only. The rows are built by next_up in board_regions.py:293-323, which reads reads['units'] alone and has no access to the graph, so the grouping cannot be written inside board_wall.py. board_regions.py and its test are added.

First, chain depth over the ready set is 42 at zero, 139 at one and 9 at two; the served graph is filtered to edges touching the drawn set, so a depth-two chain whose intermediate ancestor is closed would lose its second edge and the walk would stop early. Three ids read as disagreeing between the served graph and the ledger - 0hxck3, eaw1dy and v8jwf0 - and that is not filter loss: they were attached to k6tpep after that snapshot was taken.

SERIALIZED: this writes board_regions.py, which v8jwf0 and ffm2yp also declare. Neither is dispatched yet, so this lands first and they branch from it.

payload.value:
## Context

Reported by the operator 2026-08-22: "we have the id, priority and description, but we do not have a feature or epic name that is descriptive for the human. I cannot distinguish what each of these work items is implementing as I do not know with which feature it is connected."

A wall row today is `P1 | basicly-a4q3.10 | Carry a ranked kill list and its discriminator on a change summary`. Nothing on it says which feature that serves.

## The fact is already on the wire

Measured against the live `/snapshot.json` on 2026-08-22:

```text
parent-child edges in graph.edges : 544
distinct parents they resolve to  : 19, of which 15 are epic and 4 are feature
ready units                       : 187
  resolve to a parent             : 145  (77%)
  orphans with no parent at all   : 42   (23%)
```

The edge direction is `from` = child, `to` = parent. `units[]` already carries `title` and `type` for each of those parents. So the epic a row belongs to needs **no new producer field** - it is a fold over two arrays the document already serves.

The fourteen roots that own the ready set, by how many ready descendants each has: `e2mz` 37, `jr0l` 26, `u2hl` 20, `vkh0` 17, `tcmy` 16, `a4q3` 9, `imnu` 4, `u6jq` 3, `ze8z` 3, `a3ab` 3, `m4zv` 2, `kjc5` 2, `rn0o` 2, `agzx` 1.

## Why grouping rather than a column

Fourteen groups over 187 rows. A per-row epic column repeats the same long title 37 times for one epic and costs horizontal width the title needs. A group heading states it once. The 42 orphans become their own group, which makes a second fact visible that a column would hide: a quarter of the ready set is attached to no feature at all.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the wall renders a ready set, IT SHALL group the rows under the epic or feature each resolves to, and each heading SHALL carry that parent's own title and its ready count.
- WHEN a unit resolves to no parent, IT SHALL appear under one heading that names it as unattached, with a count.
- WHEN a chain has more than one level, THE HEADING SHALL name the root ancestor, not the immediate parent.
- WHEN the graph holds a cycle, THE FOLD SHALL terminate and the affected unit SHALL be reported as unattached rather than looping.
- WHERE grouping is applied, THE URGENCY ORDER THE WALL ALREADY RANKS BY SHALL be preserved within each group and SHALL decide the order of the groups themselves.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Render the board: `uv run basicly board --out <redacted:posix-absolute-path>`
2. Read any row under the `NEXT UP` heading.

**Observed 2026-08-22.** `P1  basicly-a4q3.10  Carry a ranked kill list and its
discriminator on a change summary`. Three fields, none of which name a feature.

**Expected.** A reader can tell which feature that row implements. `basicly-a4q3.10`
roots to `basicly-a4q3`, *Adopt the verification practices the RH campaign volume
evidences*, and nothing on the page says so.

**Control that the fact is present, not missing.** Over the same served document:
`jq '[.graph.edges[]|select(.kind=="parent-child")]|length' snapshot.json` returns a
non-zero count, and `units[]` carries a `title` and a `type` for each parent. The
fold is available; it is not performed.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_wall.py`
- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`
- `tests/test_board_wall.py`
- `tests/test_board_regions.py`
- `tests/test_board_regions_grouping.py`
- `tests/test_board_render.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `120000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: Render the live board and read the wall, checking that a row under a heading names an epic whose id is the root ancestor of that row's id in `graph.edges`, and that the unattached group's count matches the orphan count computed from the same document.

payload.description:
## Context

Measured 2026-08-08 on the five-lane pass `basicly-u2hl:bc7cc925`. **Three of five lanes
bounced on the merge queue**, and every bounce was a shared anchor no bead declares:

```text
docs/plan/implementation-plan.md   the docs-claims generated block (module count, test count)
basicly.toml                       [[verify.checks]] - .12, .14 and .15 each appended an entry
pyproject.toml                     [tool.module_size.frozen] and [tool.noqa_debt]
```

Any lane that adds a module, adds a test file, or wires a check rewrites all three.
`loop preflight` printed the warning before the pass and it was dispatched anyway:

```text
contend:   no append-only path declared ([worktree] append_only_paths)
```

## Why the existing mechanisms do not cover it

`[worktree] append_only_paths` is empty **on purpose** - its own comment records that
`CHANGELOG.md` was the whole list and that serializing every lane was the price of
detecting one collision. `basicly-4746` replaced it with one fragment file per lane, so
the collision became **impossible by construction** rather than detected. That is the
pattern to apply here; serialization is the second-best answer and is explicitly
deprecated in the config comment.

## Cost this bought

Re-dispatch does not discard work - the worktree keeps its commits - but each bounce costs
a fresh process boot and re-orientation. On `basicly-u2hl.14` the three re-dispatches were
5.6M tokens (16% of the bead) and roughly 19 minutes of a 51-minute lane (37% of its wall
clock). Pass slot utilisation was 42%.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given three concurrent lanes that each add a source module and wire a verify check, when
  the pass lands them through the merge queue, then none bounces on `basicly.toml`,
  `pyproject.toml` or `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md` - check: a test provisions three
  branches each adding one check entry and one frozen-list entry, runs the merge queue over
  all three, and asserts zero rebase conflicts and zero rework recorded.
- Given a consumer running `basicly verify`, when the checks are assembled from per-lane
  fragments rather than one array, then the same check set runs as before - check:
  `uv run basicly verify --mode full` reports the same check names and count as on the
  parent commit.

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly verify --mode full` lists the identical check set, and a three-branch merge
queue test lands all three with no bounce.

## Scope

- `basicly.toml`
- `pyproject.toml`
- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `.scripts/check_module_size.py`
- `.scripts/check_noqa_debt.py`
- `tests/test_merge.py`
- `tests/test_verify.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `120000`
- depends on: none
payload.title: Make the three shared landing anchors collision proof by construction

## Context

`docs/requirements/harness-board.md` constraint C5 states 19.1 ms for a whole snapshot build, and uses
that figure to claim the 500 ms acceptance cap carries 26x headroom. Its own per source table in the
same section already lists 16.5 ms for the **fold alone**.

`basicly-rn0o.2` measured the shipped producer on this corpus: **76.3 ms** median of 7, decomposed as
`read_ledger` 47.9 ms, `fold` 14.4 ms, `read_markers` 6.7 ms, `asks` 0.1 ms. The 19.1 ms figure
evidently excludes the log read.

The cap still holds comfortably - real headroom is about 6.5x. **The claim about the cap is what is
wrong**, and it matters because the next unit sizes its own budget against it, and because a stated
headroom of 26x invites a change that a stated 6.5x would refuse.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read constraint C5 in `docs/requirements/harness-board.md` and note the stated whole snapshot figure and the stated headroom multiple.
2. Read the per source table in the same section and note the fold figure alone.
3. Observe the fold alone is most of the stated whole.
4. Time `board_snapshot.build_document` on this corpus over several runs and take the median.
5. Observe the measured figure and the stated figure differ by about 4x, and the stated headroom multiple is correspondingly wrong.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given constraint C5 then its whole snapshot figure is consistent with its own per source decomposition and names the tree it was measured on - check: `uv run pytest tests/test_board_snapshot.py -k under_the_cap -q`
- Given the headroom multiple is stated then it follows from the corrected figure

## Scope

- `docs/requirements/harness-board.md`

## Working Set

- `docs/requirements/harness-board.md`

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_board_snapshot.py -k under_the_cap -q`

payload.description:
## Context

A bead's `## Scope` is read by two gates that want opposite things:

```text
merge scope-collision   wants the declaration COMPLETE  - every path the diff touches
decompose band          wants the declaration SMALL     - it prices what the scope READS
```

Declaring honestly for the first necessarily inflates the second. Measured on
`basicly-u2hl.14`, 2026-08-08, inside a single landing:

```text
13 scope entries   78,709 est   -> merge refused: 16 undeclared paths
27 scope entries  197,646 est   -> band ceiling 132,000 exceeded; raised to 200,000
35 scope entries  245,466 est   -> band ceiling 200,000 exceeded; raised to 248,000
```

**Nothing about the change grew.** The same diff was always that wide; only the
declaration moved. The lane chased its own tail between two gates, and the operator
raised `DEFAULT_WORKING_SET_MAX` twice in one landing to let it through — which is a
ratchet being moved by an artifact rather than by evidence.

## Why the existing beads do not cover it

`basicly-esxp` argues read-cost never predicted change cost, and `basicly-tcmy.34`
fixed the forecast unit. Both take for granted that one scope field feeds both
consumers. This bead is that assumption: even a perfect estimator over a complete
declaration reports a number that grows with declaration completeness, so the two
gates cannot both be satisfied by one field however well either is calibrated.

## Steps to Reproduce

```text
$ uv run basicly loop run <bead> --autonomy L3
[blocked] ... changed <paths> outside its declared scope ... the plan is wrong, not the merge
# declare those paths, then:
[blocked] ... completed at an estimate of N, above working_set_max M; raise it to at least K
# raise M, re-run, and the collision gate names the next undeclared path
```

Observed: two ceiling raises in one landing, neither earned by a larger change.
Expected: declaring a path completely does not make the lane look bigger.

## Shape

Separate the two readings. `## Scope` stays the ownership declaration the merge gate
reads and the collision graph learns from — complete by construction, and free. The
band reads a distinct input: either a declared working set (what the lane must *read*,
a subset), or a derived one (`basicly-agzx.2`'s AST localisation), or the diff-size
forecast `basicly-esxp` wants. Which of the three is the design question; that they
must not be the same field is the finding.

The two ceiling derivations recorded in `config.py` must then be re-read as measuring
declaration completeness, not working set, and the comment there says so.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a bead whose scope is widened to declare paths it already touched, when the
  band sizes it, then the estimate does not increase - check: a test sizes one lane at
  two declaration completenesses over an identical diff and asserts the band verdict is
  unchanged.
- Given the merge scope-collision gate, when a lane declares every path it touches,
  then it lands without a band refusal caused by that declaration - check: a test lands
  a lane whose complete declaration exceeds the old ceiling and asserts no ceiling
  violation is recorded.

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly loop preflight <epic>` reports the same band verdict for a bead before
and after its scope is completed against the merge gate's own finding.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/decompose.py`
- `src/basicly/working_set.py`
- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `tests/test_decompose.py`
- `tests/test_working_set.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `110000`
- depends on: none

payload.description:
## Context
When eight agent sessions write to one vault clone at once, I want each local write to be accepted quickly, so an agent swarm does not get refused writes it must retry.

## Finding
2026-11-17, probe of test_proof_t_agents_eight_sessions_in_three_worktrees_land_each_event_once on 2 CPUs (1 failure in 36 runs): 1 of 1000 comment writes exited 1 with {refused: another writer holds .../pending-r/.events.lock after 5.0s}. The refusal is safe and named, and the caller sees it. It caused the 999 of 1000 failure in quality-gates 43965947002 because the test agent ignored the exit code; the test now retries refused writes. Why a local write waits more than 5 s for the pending-view lock is not yet measured.

## Fix
Measure the pending-view lock hold time under 8 sessions and shorten the critical section, so a local write is not refused under that load. Not claimed.
payload.title: Keep a local vault write from waiting over five seconds for the pending view lock under eight sessions

payload.description:
## CORRECTED 2026-08-13 — read this before the text below
The defect holds verbatim: `loop.py:867-879` still passes only the issue id, with no
requirement, scope, plan or prior finding. **The evidence and the remedy are both stale.**

**The 254x is two incomparable populations.** Re-measured over 346 records on 2026-08-13 it is
now 320x - and it compares a `decide` dispatch averaging **12 seconds** to a `lane` averaging
**979 seconds**. That is a one-turn classification against a multi-hour build, so it cannot
isolate briefing from work type. This repo's own recorded lesson is "a cost prior from the
wrong population"; do not cite this ratio as the cost of a short prompt. The causal claim that
a ~1.1M-token floor is "bought by the instruction" has **no instrument behind it**: there is no
per-lane split between context acquisition and implementation.

**Two mechanisms are now recorded as if they were one fix.** `factory-loop.md` section 8.3
still names the engine-assembled durable brief. `implementation-plan.md:224` substitutes
`--resume --fork-session`, calling the floor "a cache miss, not tokens". These are different
designs with different costs and the choice must be made explicitly, not inherited.

**The fork figure does not hold in our shape.** Probed on claude 2.1.231, 2026-08-13: 19.06x
same-directory, but the denominator is the ~21k-token host floor, not a repo corpus - against a
lane's 8.66M mean that floor is 0.24% of a lane. And a fork from a **different working
directory degrades to 5.4x**, because cwd and a git-status snapshot sit inside the cached
prefix, worktrees of the same repository included. Every lane is dispatched at
`cwd=worktree_path` (`supervise.py:2623`), so fork-per-lane plus worktree-per-lane **is** the
degraded case. See `basicly-w20y` for the documents-side correction.

**Acceptance criterion 3 was unmeasurable when written** and is now measurable:
`basicly-i4gg` (closed 2026-08-13) landed the claude cache split that a before/after ratio
needs.

---

## Context

**A dispatched lane is told to go and read; a dispatched decider is handed its corpus. The
same model on the same repo costs 254x more for the first.** Measured 2026-08-08 over the
whole of `.basicly/usage/run-records.json`:

```text
phase    n    mean tokens   mean $   mean s   failed
lane    77      8,124,617    6.28      942    16/93 = 17.2%
build   28     11,564,149    8.70     1163     4/153 =  2.6%
decide  24         31,991    0.23       14     5/29  = 17.2%
```

`loop.dispatch_prompt` (`loop.py:858`) is ~90 words and passes **only the issue id**:

```text
"You are in a git worktree dedicated to the tracked issue <id>. Read AGENTS.md for the
 repo rules, run `br show <id>` for the requirement and acceptance criteria, implement
 the work, and commit it on the current branch referencing that issue id. ..."
```

No requirement text, no scope, no plan, no architecture, no prior finding. The prompt
*instructs* the agent to rebuild what the dispatching session already holds, and the
~1.1M-token floor every lane pays before its first edit is bought by that instruction.

Observed cost of the same waste twice in one session: `u2hl.15`'s lane independently
re-derived pyright's dot-directory behaviour that had been measured, written down and
committed to its own bead an hour earlier.

Per unit of output, the floor dominates small work: `u2hl.16` cost **\$0.077 per changed
line**, `u2hl.14` **\$0.010**.

## What this bead is NOT

It is **not** "make the prompt longer". `factory-design.md` §D6 records a deliberate
decision that every dispatch pays fresh context priming, grounded in Laban et al.'s
measured **-39% on multi-turn** degradation. That decision is about *conversation* history,
not about *facts the engine already knows*, and this bead must not overturn it by accident.

The docs already contain the shape that resolves the tension: the **report file**
(`agent-roster-design.md:664-670`, `gates-and-rework-design.md:219-235`) — an agent
inherits through a durable, structured artifact rather than through a replayed window.
`basicly-u2hl.18` already shipped two such artifacts (`implementation-plan`,
`change-summary`) as typed records, so the mechanism exists and has a schema.

## Shape

Give the dispatch prompt a **brief assembled by the engine** from what it already has:
the bead's requirement and acceptance criteria (already read to gate it), the declared
scope, the plan artifact, and any finding recorded on the bead. Every one of those is a
tracker read the engine performs anyway.

Two constraints from this repo's own measurements:
- **Selection, not serialisation** (D21): `br ready --json` costs 36.9% of a lane and its
  five-field projection costs 1.7%. Assemble the brief from named fields, never by pasting
  a payload.
- **Our own vocabulary, not `br`'s** (D22): `br` is being removed; the brief names our
  record fields so only the adapter changes at the flip.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a dispatched lane, when its prompt is built, then the requirement, acceptance
  criteria, declared scope and plan artifact are present in the prompt - check: a test
  asserts each field appears in `dispatch_prompt` output for a fixture bead.
- Given the same bead dispatched twice, when the briefs are compared, then they are
  identical - check: a test asserts prompt determinism, preserving D9's diffability.
- Given a measured pair of lanes before and after, when mean tokens-to-first-edit are
  compared, then the briefed lane is lower - check: recorded on the bead from
  `run-records.json`, with the before figure taken in base first.

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly loop run <bead> --runner manual` prints the brief the lane would receive,
and it contains the bead's acceptance criteria and scope rather than an instruction to go
and read them.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/br.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `120000`
- depends on: none
payload.title: Hand a dispatched agent the context the session already holds

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Trigger

When a lane is dispatched to build a unit of work, I want it to receive the requirement, scope and any recorded plan the engine already holds, so I can stop paying a lane to rebuild context a session already read.

## CORRECTED 2026-08-13 — read this before the text below
The defect holds verbatim: `loop.py:867-879` still passes only the issue id, with no
requirement, scope, plan or prior finding. **The evidence and the remedy are both stale.**

**The 254x is two incomparable populations.** Re-measured over 346 records on 2026-08-13 it is
now 320x - and it compares a `decide` dispatch averaging **12 seconds** to a `lane` averaging
**979 seconds**. That is a one-turn classification against a multi-hour build, so it cannot
isolate briefing from work type. This repo's own recorded lesson is "a cost prior from the
wrong population"; do not cite this ratio as the cost of a short prompt. The causal claim that
a ~1.1M-token floor is "bought by the instruction" has **no instrument behind it**: there is no
per-lane split between context acquisition and implementation.

**Two mechanisms are now recorded as if they were one fix.** `factory-loop.md` section 8.3
still names the engine-assembled durable brief. `implementation-plan.md:224` substitutes
`--resume --fork-session`, calling the floor "a cache miss, not tokens". These are different
designs with different costs and the choice must be made explicitly, not inherited.

**The fork figure does not hold in our shape.** Probed on claude 2.1.231, 2026-08-13: 19.06x
same-directory, but the denominator is the ~21k-token host floor, not a repo corpus - against a
lane's 8.66M mean that floor is 0.24% of a lane. And a fork from a **different working
directory degrades to 5.4x**, because cwd and a git-status snapshot sit inside the cached
prefix, worktrees of the same repository included. Every lane is dispatched at
`cwd=worktree_path` (`supervise.py:2623`), so fork-per-lane plus worktree-per-lane **is** the
degraded case. See `basicly-w20y` for the documents-side correction.

**Acceptance criterion 3 was unmeasurable when written** and is now measurable:
`basicly-i4gg` (closed 2026-08-13) landed the claude cache split that a before/after ratio
needs.

---

## Context

**A dispatched lane is told to go and read; a dispatched decider is handed its corpus. The
same model on the same repo costs 254x more for the first.** Measured 2026-08-08 over the
whole of `.basicly/usage/run-records.json`:

```text
phase    n    mean tokens   mean $   mean s   failed
lane    77      8,124,617    6.28      942    16/93 = 17.2%
build   28     11,564,149    8.70     1163     4/153 =  2.6%
decide  24         31,991    0.23       14     5/29  = 17.2%
```

`loop.dispatch_prompt` (`loop.py:858`) is ~90 words and passes **only the issue id**:

```text
"You are in a git worktree dedicated to the tracked issue <id>. Read AGENTS.md for the
 repo rules, run `br show <id>` for the requirement and acceptance criteria, implement
 the work, and commit it on the current branch referencing that issue id. ..."
```

No requirement text, no scope, no plan, no architecture, no prior finding. The prompt
*instructs* the agent to rebuild what the dispatching session already holds, and the
~1.1M-token floor every lane pays before its first edit is bought by that instruction.

Observed cost of the same waste twice in one session: `u2hl.15`'s lane independently
re-derived pyright's dot-directory behaviour that had been measured, written down and
committed to its own bead an hour earlier.

Per unit of output, the floor dominates small work: `u2hl.16` cost **\$0.077 per changed
line**, `u2hl.14` **\$0.010**.

## What this bead is NOT

It is **not** "make the prompt longer". `factory-design.md` §D6 records a deliberate
decision that every dispatch pays fresh context priming, grounded in Laban et al.'s
measured **-39% on multi-turn** degradation. That decision is about *conversation* history,
not about *facts the engine already knows*, and this bead must not overturn it by accident.

The docs already contain the shape that resolves the tension: the **report file**
(`agent-roster-design.md:664-670`, `gates-and-rework-design.md:219-235`) — an agent
inherits through a durable, structured artifact rather than through a replayed window.
`basicly-u2hl.18` already shipped two such artifacts (`implementation-plan`,
`change-summary`) as typed records, so the mechanism exists and has a schema.

## Shape

Give the dispatch prompt a **brief assembled by the engine** from what it already has:
the bead's requirement and acceptance criteria (already read to gate it), the declared
scope, the plan artifact, and any finding recorded on the bead. Every one of those is a
tracker read the engine performs anyway.

Two constraints from this repo's own measurements:
- **Selection, not serialisation** (D21): `br ready --json` costs 36.9% of a lane and its
  five-field projection costs 1.7%. Assemble the brief from named fields, never by pasting
  a payload.
- **Our own vocabulary, not `br`'s** (D22): `br` is being removed; the brief names our
  record fields so only the adapter changes at the flip.

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly loop run <bead> --runner manual` prints the brief the lane would receive,
and it contains the bead's acceptance criteria and scope rather than an instruction to go
and read them.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/br.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `120000`
- depends on: none

## Earlier acceptance text (the acceptance field is authoritative)

- Given a dispatched lane, when its prompt is built, then the requirement, acceptance
  criteria, declared scope and plan artifact are present in the prompt - check: a test
  asserts each field appears in `dispatch_prompt` output for a fixture bead.
- Given the same bead dispatched twice, when the briefs are compared, then they are
  identical - check: a test asserts prompt determinism, preserving D9's diffability.
- Given a measured pair of lanes before and after, when mean tokens-to-first-edit are
  compared, then the briefed lane is lower - check: recorded on the bead from
  `run-records.json`, with the before figure taken in base first.
